items.title: Motorcycles are notoriously dangerous. Could electric motorcycles actually change that?
items.summary:
There’s no particularly comfortable way to talk about motorcycle safety. Motorcycles are dangerous. All the statistics point to the fact that per mile, motorcycles are significantly more dangerous. And as someone who promotes them as a better alternative to large cars and trucks for many trips, it’s an uncomfortable reality that must be grappled with.

But that simple statement also hides something important. Not all motorcycles, riders, or riding behaviors carry the same risk. And as a new generation of smaller electric motorcycles begins to emerge, I think there’s an interesting question worth asking: Could electric motorcycles inadvertently make motorcycling safer?

more…

items.title: REO Targets 5,000-Pound Max Towing for Its Tiny Four-Cylinder Trucks
items.summary:
Call me cautiously optimistic about REO Industries and the Runabout family of vehicles it hopes to build. They’re still a long way from production, but in theory, they should be pretty sweet. Not only does the startup want to sell its simple trucks for $21,500 and up; it also wants to build them with simple four-cylinder engines, manual transmissions, and mechanical 4×4. And in speaking with REO Founder and CEO Zach De Bernardi, The Drive learned that they could also tow up to 5,000 pounds—quite a bit more than the Ford Maverick.

While flipping through REO’s press photos showing the truck that was styled by Frank Stephenson Design, we noticed a T4X single-cab model pulling a 20-foot fiberglass boat on a tandem-axle trailer. We estimated the weight to be 5,000 pounds or more with a little bit of napkin math, and De Bernardi confirmed that’s the goal. He added that the Toyota Hilux Champ can do 5,500 pounds, so it set the benchmark. Supposedly, the REO Runabout will have larger wheels than the ‘Yota, so it can also fit bigger brakes.

As for payload, REO targets a max capacity of 2,500 pounds. REO Industries 

It’s encouraging to see a startup value such strong fundamentals. REO isn’t interested in small-displacement, big-power turbo engines to compensate for anything. Instead, it seems comfortable embracing less impressive stats if that results in greater dependability—500,000 miles is the goal.

Take, for example, REO’s decision to run a solid axle instead of independent front suspension. “First and foremost, this vehicle is designed as a truck,” De Bernardi told The…
items.t: REO Targets 5,000-Pound Max Towing for Its Tiny Four-Cylinder Trucks

items.title: REO Wants to Fight Ford and Slate With These Oh-So-Simple Work Trucks
items.summary:
I don’t know about you, but I’m glad to be alive for the small truck renaissance we’re enjoying. Don’t get me wrong— I like big trucks as much as the next guy , but even I can admit they aren’t always practical. Ford and Slate are bringing affordable pickups to market in the next few years, but as some people can’t help but hate, they’re both electric. REO might be good news for those folks, though, as the startup promises real-deal trucks on the cheap with naturally aspirated four-cylinder engines, manual transmissions, and solid front axles.

Called the Runabout, this rig comes in three different flavors: the T4X work truck, T4C crew cab, and S4C family SUV. We’ve known about them for a while, but until now, they were just names on paper. REO has since partnered with Frank Stephenson Design—led by the fella who penned the reborn Mini, as well as the McLaren P1—to style its machinery. According to the snazzy sketches REO sent over, the trucks’ exterior is based on a bison. It’s called biomimicry, and it’s everywhere in design. ( For what it’s worth, Frank Stephenson says the sailfish was his main inspo for the P1 .)

REO Industries 

What’s most remarkable about these REO Runabout models is their intentional simplicity. All of them should ride on the same ladder frame, with the same engines, the same mechanical 4×4 systems, and the same transmission options. Now, not all of them will be manuals, but those that are will be about $1,500 cheaper than their self-shifting counterparts. REO’s CEO and Founder, Zach De Bernardi, explained to The Drive that they’re still…

items.title: Ford’s Rouge Facility Was Targeted by Massive Employee-Aided Theft Ring
items.summary:
Ford’s Rouge assembly plant has been identified as one of the sources of parts sold online as part of a multi-year, multi-million-dollar heist operation run by four people (including a Ford employee). The ring was busted last May after tens of thousands of dollars worth of stolen, brand-new parts were identified in the inventory of an eBay storefront. 

The discovery led to raids on warehouses and homes in Detroit and the suburbs of Dearborn and Canton last year. Police were seen recovering entire pallets of OEM parts ranging from body panels to entire axle assemblies. 

Ford’s Rouge Factory in Dearborn was the source of roughly $80,000 in stolen parts , Automotive News reported Monday. Using their employee connection to gain access to the facility, the ring pilfered parts over the course of six consecutive Saturday nights in the spring 0f 2025. 

Rouge was not the only source of stolen inventory. Dearborn Police Chief Issa Shahin told Fox 2 Detroit last May that the thieves also hit Ford facilities in Wayne and Flat Rock over a period of at least two years. The details of those thefts were not included in the latest report. 

During a Nov. 10 news conference, Wayne Country Prosecutor Kym Worthy told media that the total value of the property stolen while the ring was in operation is much larger than what was listed in the charges against the four alleged ringleaders (Badr Kahil, 63, Aiman Kahil, 25, and Firas Kahil, 36, and Wissam Faraj, 35). 

Warehouses in Detroit filled “from the floor to the ceiling” with brand-new Ford parts ranging from body panels, Shahin said.…
items.t: Ford’s Rouge Facility Was Targeted by Massive Employee-Aided Theft Ring

items.title: Mercedes’ Hands-Free Driving Assist Tackled San Fran’s Steepest Streets, Cyclists, Traffic. Here’s How It Went
items.summary:
Back in the summer of 2022, I went to Germany to test Mercedes-Benz’s Level 3 hands-free driving system, and it impressed me then. I could read The Drive while the car drove itself down the road, and even play video games from the center touchscreen. However, the tech was heavily regulated for highway operation only and limited to a paltry 37 mph. Fast forward to last week, and I climbed into a U.S.-spec 2027 Mercedes GLC 400 Electric to see what the brand’s new point-to-point Level 2 hands-free assist could do in a busy metropolis like San Francisco.

Dubbed MB Drive Assist Pro and Hands-Free Highway Assist, these latest tech offerings from Mercedes allow drivers in California to take their hands off the wheel while navigating urban environments and eligible controlled-access highways. And unlike before, you can do it at speeds up to 85 mph.

Mercedes-Benz 

You can watch the video below to see how I fared through the busy streets of the Bay Area, including typical big-city treats like double-parked cars, road construction, cyclists, and, of course, lots of pedestrians. Most impressively, however, was the system’s confidence and fluidity in its decisions, always feeling sure of its movements, which is more I can say for rival systems out there.

MB Drive Assist Pro uses 27 sensing components—including 10 cameras, five radar sensors, and 12 ultrasonic sensors—and a high-performance computer delivering up to 254 Tera Operations Per Second to process the incoming data. As you’ll see in the video, the dual screens (gauge cluster and infotainment) show what the car sees and…

Regulators were already looking into some recent Honda vehicles reportedly exhibiting this behavior, but this particular group does not appear to share their root cause, and the same repairs don’t seem to apply. BMW is recalling more than 720,000 vehicles across a range of nameplates for short-circuit-prone water pumps that could cause fires. items.title: This 1968 Shelby Mustang GT350 Is Seriously Rare. That Didn’t Stop the Owner From Supercharging It
items.summary:
When it comes to investment-grade collector vehicles, there are few safer bets than a 1960s muscle car. And if you want to hedge your bet, a Shelby Mustang is a good way to go. The original Mustang is legendary, the Ford partnership with Shelby American even more so. But despite the potential value tied up in this 1968 Shelby Mustang GT350 convertible’s sheetmetal and woodgrain dash and door-panel appliqués, the selling owner wasn’t afraid of modifying it.

Currently up for auction on Bring a Trailer , this car is one of just 404 GT350 convertibles built for the 1968 model year. It was restored in 2020, now shows 32,000 miles, and has the factory-correct 302-cubic-inch V8. But that engine is now topped with a Paxton supercharger installed after the seller bought the car. The seller also swapped the original three-speed automatic transmission for a five-speed manual. The supercharger is at least a period-correct modification, but no such excuse can be made for the modern Flowmaster exhaust system. All the removed original parts are included with the sale.

B 

Credit: Bring a Trailer 

The Mustang may have had the biggest launch of any new car in history, but Ford wanted to keep that momentum going. And under its Total Performance program, the automaker used racing as its primary marketing tool. So it asked Shelby to turn the Mustang into a race car, and the GT350 was born. The original 1965 model was intended for SCCA racing, but Ford and Shelby quickly realized that customers wanted a more refined road car with sporty styling more than a track toy.

items.title: Can’t Pass Emissions With Your Pre-OBD-II Car? Have Claude Tune It for You
items.summary:
Artificial intelligence has been crowned as the next big thing by whoever makes those decisions. It’s now being implemented across the auto industry , and despite all the hype, we mostly seem to be finding out what it can’t do , and that it requires a lot of memory to achieve even that disappointing level of performance. But one YouTuber claims to have found a very good use for Claude.

Muhammad Zulali has a 1994 Jeep Cherokee that failed California emissions tests. Because it’s a 1994 model, this XJ Cherokee doesn’t have an OBD-II port, so Zulali couldn’t plug in a generic scanning tool to look for trouble codes. There was a Chrysler-specific scanning tool compatible with vehicles from this model year, but it’s hard to find these days and doesn’t provide much information anyway, Zulali explains in the video.

Muhammad Zulali via YouTube 

Looking for an alternative way to read data from the car’s onboard computer, Zulali says he asked Claude, which identified the computer’s communication protocol and suggested using an Arduino Nano to translate it. Arduino makes open-source microcontrollers that are prized in the maker community for their flexibility, and they can come in handy when doing engine swaps involving different manufacturers’ computer controls as well. This one cost just $3.

That allowed Claude to take readings from the Cherokee’s computer, but the first ones created more questions than answers. Thinking that low fuel pressure might be the issue, Zulali began testing that—and found out that Claude could do more than just passively read data. He said the model…

items.title: A Ford Maverick Will Fit a Gnarly Twin-Turbo V8—With a Whole Lot of Work
items.summary:
When the Ford Maverick arrived in 2021, it revived the compact truck segment that has long been a favorite of tuners and customizers. So it’s not surprising that we’ve seen quite a few modified Mavericks in the short time this pickup has been on sale. Yet there’s one obvious thing no one attempted until now: a V8 swap.

Tucci Hot Rods finally rectified that at the 2026 SEMA show, where it unveiled a 2022 Maverick with a twin-turbo Coyote V8. If you’re not familiar with this Upstate New York shop, it was one of the first that Ford partnered with on Maverick SEMA builds back in 2021. Tucci’s first go was a 2.0-liter EcoBoost truck with 3D-printed parts that gave it a serious street-truck vibe. Ford cited that build as one of the inspirations for the Maverick Lobo , in fact. Now, Tucci has Coyote-swapped that truck.

Credit: Tucci Hot Rods via Facebook 

“When we originally built the truck in 2021 for Ford, it was a pre-production vehicle. The build went over really well, and afterward, we joked that we should Coyote-swap it,” Tucci Hot Rods owner Dave Tucci told Ford Muscle . “Eventually, that joke turned into a real plan.”

As detailed in a post by Engine Swap Depot , Tucci paired Ford’s ubiquitous 5.0-liter V8 with a pair of Hellion 62 millimeter turbos. The engine was also treated to a new intake manifold, oil pan, and fuel rails, while the exhaust was routed through the Maverick’s front fender vents using custom 3D-printed pieces. The setup is good for up to 1,200 horsepower.

Credit: Tucci Hot Rods via Facebook 

The engine is connected to a ZF 8HP70 eight-speed…
items.t: A Ford Maverick Will Fit a Gnarly Twin-Turbo V8—With a Whole Lot of Work
